source.paper_title: RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables

summary: RUNLTS introduces register-value components to the statistical corrector (SC) to exploit correlations between branch directions and recently produced register values. By digesting completed register values into 12-bit signatures and mapping logical registers to specific banks, the predictor selects the digest of the most 'useful' available register per bank at prediction time. These digests are fed into hashed weight tables to produce a prediction bias. It is particularly effective immediately after a branch misprediction because many in-flight instructions have finished execution, exposing more values to the predictor.

state.name: register_status_table
state.organization: 1 entry per logical register, covering integer, FP, and flags
state.entry_format: valid (1 bit), payload (14 bits: either ROB tag or 12-bit digest), decay_ctr (8 bits)
state.indexing: indexed by logical register ID [0 to num_logical_regs-1]

state.name: sr_usefulness_tables
state.organization: 8 banks, 3 tables per bank (UT0, UT1, UT2)
state.indexing: hashed by skewed functions of PC and register ID

state.name: sr_prediction_tables
state.organization: 8 banks, 3 tables per bank (WT0, WT1, WT2)
state.indexing: hashed by skewed functions of PC and 12-bit register digest

state.name: sr_inflight_state
state.entry_format: For each of the 8 banks: valid (1 bit), selected_reg_for_ut (4 bits), best_digest (12 bits), max_usefulness (6 bits)
state.indexing: indexed by branch ROB index or sequential branch tag modulo inflight_branches

algorithms.name: decode
algorithms.trigger: decode time of an instruction that writes a register
algorithms.notes: Tracks which instruction is the latest producer for a logical register.

algorithms.name: execute_complete
algorithms.trigger: completion of an instruction that writes a register
algorithms.pseudocode:
if register_status_table[inst.dest_reg].valid == false and register_status_table[inst.dest_reg].payload == inst.rob_index:
  digest = 0
  if inst.type == INT:
    lz = min(leading_zeros_or_ones(inst.value), 63)
    tz = min(trailing_zeros_or_ones(inst.value), 63)
    digest = ((inst.value & 0x3F) << 6) ^ (lz << 3) ^ tz
  elif inst.type == FP:
    if inst.opcode_width == 16: digest = (inst.value >> 13) & 0x7
    elif inst.opcode_width == 32: digest = (inst.value >> 26) & 0x3F
    else: digest = (inst.value >> 55) & 0x1FF
  elif inst.type == FLAG:
    flags = inst.value & 0xF
    digest = (flags << 8) | (flags << 4) | flags
  
  register_status_table[inst.dest_reg].payload = digest
  register_status_table[inst.dest_reg].valid = true
  register_status_table[inst.dest_reg].decay_ctr = decay_cycles - 1
algorithms.notes: Generates a 12-bit digest from the computed value and makes it available for prediction.

algorithms.name: decay_digests
algorithms.notes: Invalidates stale digests to prevent degrading prediction accuracy.

algorithms.name: predict
algorithms.pseudocode:
sR = 0
inflight = sr_inflight_state[inflight_idx]
for b in 0 to (num_banks - 1):
  max_u = -32
  best_reg = 0
  valid_regs = []
  
  for i in 0 to 8:
    reg = b + i * 8
    if reg < num_logical_regs and register_status_table[reg].valid:
      valid_regs.append(reg)
      idx0 = hash_ut(PC, reg, 0) % ut0_entries
      idx1 = hash_ut(PC, reg, 1) % ut1_entries
      idx2 = hash_ut(PC, reg, 2) % ut2_entries
      u = sr_usefulness_tables.UT0[reg][idx0] + sr_usefulness_tables.UT1[reg][idx1] + sr_usefulness_tables.UT2[reg][idx2]
      if u > max_u:
        max_u = u
        best_reg = reg
        
  if len(valid_regs) > 0:
    inflight.bank[b].valid = true
    inflight.bank[b].selected_reg_for_ut = randomly_select(valid_regs)
    inflight.bank[b].best_digest = register_status_table[best_reg].payload
    inflight.bank[b].max_usefulness = max_u
    
    idx0 = hash_wt(PC, inflight.bank[b].best_digest, 0) % wt0_entries
    idx1 = hash_wt(PC, inflight.bank[b].best_digest, 1) % wt1_entries
    idx2 = hash_wt(PC, inflight.bank[b].best_digest, 2) % wt2_entries
    pred = sr_prediction_tables.WT0[b][idx0] + sr_prediction_tables.WT1[b][idx1] + sr_prediction_tables.WT2[b][idx2]
    
    if max_u >= usefulness_threshold:
      sR = sR + pred * usefulness_multiplier
  else:
    inflight.bank[b].valid = false
return sR
algorithms.notes: Selects the most useful available register in each bank and sums their weighted predictions.

algorithms.name: update
algorithms.pseudocode:
inflight = sr_inflight_state[inflight_idx]
for b in 0 to (num_banks - 1):
  if inflight.bank[b].valid:
    reg_ut = inflight.bank[b].selected_reg_for_ut
    idx0_ut = hash_ut(PC, reg_ut, 0) % ut0_entries
    idx1_ut = hash_ut(PC, reg_ut, 1) % ut1_entries
    idx2_ut = hash_ut(PC, reg_ut, 2) % ut2_entries
    
    if branch_correct:
      sr_usefulness_tables.UT0[reg_ut][idx0_ut] = saturate_add(sr_usefulness_tables.UT0[reg_ut][idx0_ut], 1)
      sr_usefulness_tables.UT1[reg_ut][idx1_ut] = saturate_add(sr_usefulness_tables.UT1[reg_ut][idx1_ut], 1)
      sr_usefulness_tables.UT2[reg_ut][idx2_ut] = saturate_add(sr_usefulness_tables.UT2[reg_ut][idx2_ut], 1)
    else:
      sr_usefulness_tables.UT0[reg_ut][idx0_ut] = saturate_sub(sr_usefulness_tables.UT0[reg_ut][idx0_ut], 1)
      sr_usefulness_tables.UT1[reg_ut][idx1_ut] = saturate_sub(sr_usefulness_tables.UT1[reg_ut][idx1_ut], 1)
      sr_usefulness_tables.UT2[reg_ut][idx2_ut] = saturate_sub(sr_usefulness_tables.UT2[reg_ut][idx2_ut], 1)
      
    digest = inflight.bank[b].best_digest
    idx0_wt = hash_wt(PC, digest, 0) % wt0_entries
    idx1_wt = hash_wt(PC, digest, 1) % wt1_entries
    idx2_wt = hash_wt(PC, digest, 2) % wt2_entries
    
    if branch_taken:
      sr_prediction_tables.WT0[b][idx0_wt] = saturate_add(sr_prediction_tables.WT0[b][idx0_wt], 1)
      sr_prediction_tables.WT1[b][idx1_wt] = saturate_add(sr_prediction_tables.WT1[b][idx1_wt], 1)
      sr_prediction_tables.WT2[b][idx2_wt] = saturate_add(sr_prediction_tables.WT2[b][idx2_wt], 1)
    else:
      sr_prediction_tables.WT0[b][idx0_wt] = saturate_sub(sr_prediction_tables.WT0[b][idx0_wt], 1)
      sr_prediction_tables.WT1[b][idx1_wt] = saturate_sub(sr_prediction_tables.WT1[b][idx1_wt], 1)
      sr_prediction_tables.WT2[b][idx2_wt] = saturate_sub(sr_prediction_tables.WT2[b][idx2_wt], 1)
algorithms.notes: Updates UT based on overall prediction correctness, and WT based on actual branch outcome.

algorithms.name: mispredict_recovery
algorithms.notes: Removes tracking tags for instructions that were squashed and will never complete, leaving the register invalid.

resource_accounting.storage_breakdown: sR usefulness tables (UT) = 9360 bits; sR prediction tables (WT) = 43008 bits; register_status_table = 1495 bits; sr_inflight_state = 23552 bits.
resource_accounting.logic_cost_notes: The paper claims 53863 bits for the sR component (Table 3), which covers the WT, UT, and register status table. It does not budget for the per-branch state needed to carry the prediction-time chosen digests and randomly chosen registers down to the commit-time update. I have added `sr_inflight_state` to hold this, accounting for 23552 bits (assuming 128 in-flight branches), making the total 77415 bits.
resource_accounting.budget_donors: Bimodal predictor or high banks of the tagged table

parameters.name: algorithms_1_pseudocode_variant
parameters.question: When a 64-bit INT register value is 0x0 or ~0ULL, the leading/trailing count is 64, which requires 7 bits. The digest fields are only 6 bits wide. Should the count be saturated at 63, or wrapped/masked so that 64 becomes 0?

parameters.name: algorithms_1_pseudocode_variant_2
parameters.question: Where do the selected FP bits sit inside the 12-bit digest? The figure implies right-aligned (low-order), but left-aligned is equally consistent and keeps the exponent in the high bits.

unit_tests.name: decode_invalidates_register
unit_tests.given: An instruction is decoded that writes to logical register R8 with ROB index 10.
unit_tests.expect: The decode algorithm sets register_status_table[8].valid to false and its payload to 10.

unit_tests.name: execute_computes_int_digest
unit_tests.given: An INT instruction with ROB index 10 writing to R8 completes with value 0x0.
unit_tests.expect: The execute_complete algorithm sets register_status_table[8].valid to true and decay_ctr to 256 (decay_cycles). The payload receives the INT digest: leading zeros=63 (saturated), trailing zeros=63, value[5:0]=0, resulting in (0 << 6) ^ (63 << 3) ^ 63 = 0x1FF.

unit_tests.name: decay_counter_expires
unit_tests.given: R8 is valid in the register_status_table with decay_ctr = 2. Advance the pipeline by decoding 2 subsequent instructions.
unit_tests.expect: The decay_digests algorithm executes twice. register_status_table[8].decay_ctr reaches 0, and register_status_table[8].valid becomes false, rendering the register unavailable for prediction.

unit_tests.name: predict_selects_most_useful
unit_tests.given: At branch lookup, bank 0 has R0 and R8 valid. sr_usefulness_tables (UT0, UT1, UT2) for R0 sum to 10. For R8 they sum to 15. usefulness_threshold is 0.
unit_tests.expect: The predict algorithm evaluates max_usefulness to 15, selects R8's digest for sr_prediction_tables (WT0, WT1, WT2) lookup, and saves R8's max_usefulness and digest in sr_inflight_state. The sR prediction accumulates the WT output multiplied by usefulness_multiplier.

unit_tests.name: update_trains_tables
unit_tests.given: At branch commit, sr_inflight_state for bank 0 is valid, with selected_reg_for_ut = R0. The branch is taken and correctly predicted 31 times consecutively.
unit_tests.expect: The update algorithm increments the signed counters in sr_prediction_tables and sr_usefulness_tables 31 times. They reach their saturation limit of 31 (for 6-bit signed counters) and remain at 31 on further correct predictions.

unit_tests.name: mispredict_recovery_clears_tag
unit_tests.given: Instruction with ROB index 20 writing to R16 was decoded but not completed. register_status_table[16] is invalid with payload (tag) = 20. A branch misprediction squashes ROB index 20.
unit_tests.expect: The mispredict_recovery algorithm observes the squashed tag, sets register_status_table[16].payload to 0, and leaves valid as false.

open_questions: Figure 5(c) U1: Does the usefulness multiplier activate at usefulness >= 0 or > 0? Assumed >= 0 (usefulness_threshold=0). Also assumed it outputs 0 when no register is valid in the bank.
Figure 5(c) U2: Are the three UTs indexed by three different skewed hashes of the PC, or one hash with the bank index folded in? Assumed three different skewed hashes of PC and register ID.
[/host_interfaces/1] Figure 6(b) U5: Is the FP format classified by opcode width or NaN-boxing? Assumed width supplied by opcode.

[/unit_tests/5/expect] Section 5: How is the register status table recovered on a squash? Assumed that entries for squashed instructions simply remain invalid by clearing their ROB tags, rather than restoring a full pre-branch checkpoint.

Section 4.2: How exactly are the usefulness tables (UT) updated during training? Assumed the randomly selected register's UT entry is incremented if the overall branch was correctly predicted, and decremented otherwise.

Section 4.2: The paper requires UT entries to hold an eight- (or nine-) element vector of weights to enable selection without adding extra memory ports. The spec currently defines a single 6-bit counter per entry and indexes by register ID. How should the single-port vector layout be reconciled with the hashed lookup?

[/resource_accounting] The total storage budget for the sR component is 77415 bits, including 23552 bits of inflight state. The paper says: "| sR: Register | 6 x (2^7 + 2^8 + 2^9) x 8 | 6 x 65 x (2^3 + 2^3 + 2^3) | { valid (1), payload (14), | 53863 |" The correction did not land, so this field still says what it said -- resolve it before implementing.
[/unit_tests/3/expect] Does the register prediction gate open at usefulness >= 0, usefulness > 0, or some other threshold?

[/algorithms/1/pseudocode] Where do the selected FP bits sit inside the 12-bit digest? The figure implies right-aligned (low-order), but left-aligned is equally consistent and keeps the exponent in the high bits.
[/algorithms/1/pseudocode] The execute_complete algorithm reads inst.type == FLAG, but no other algorithm produces this type. Which stage produces FLAG, and what exactly does its payload hold?

[source I3: Figure 5 (c) Proposed Register Components] the input marks this INFERRED -- a reading of the figure's layout that the paper never states -- so whatever the spec derives from it is an assumption and not a fact: Which logical register belongs to which bank is a reading of the layout. Bank 0's input is labelled with the registers R0, R8, R16, ..., R64, so banks are strided by 8 and bank b holds {b, b+8, ..., b+56}; that makes bank 0 the only nine-register bank, because R64 has no stride-8 partners. The figure states the list for bank 0 only and says the other banks are "identical", so the mapping for banks 1 ... 7 is deduced, not printed.

[source I4: Figure 6 (a) INT registers] the input marks this INFERRED -- a reading of the figure's layout that the paper never states -- so whatever the spec derives from it is an assumption and not a fact: The three fields overlap and are XORed together into one 12-bit digest: bit positions 11 ... 6 hold Value[5:0], the leading-count field spans positions 8 ... 3, and the trailing-count field spans positions 5 ... 0. The drawing stacks three labelled bars with "+" between them; that the "+" denotes XOR of overlapping fields rather than concatenation of disjoint ones is a reading of the layout. Section 4.2's prose says only that the digest "encodes the count of leading zeros (or ones), the count of trailing zeros (or ones), and the six least significant bits".
